subject: Intermittent p99 spikes during autoscale warmstart — AcuPay production
messages:
From: Helen Zhou <hzhou@acupay.com>
To: support@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: ops@acupay.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Intermittent p99 spikes during morning batch — AcuPay production

Hi team,

We saw recurring latency spikes this morning between ~08:30-09:05 ET that pushed p95 -> 1.2s and p99 -> 9-12s for our Checkout API calls routed through Redwood hosted inference. Around the same time we also observed an uptick in 502s (roughly 0.7% of requests) and a dip in throughput as autoscaling events kicked in. Please see attached screenshot of the latency graph and a small sample of error responses.

This is impacting our morning processing window for batch tokenization and some customers are seeing slowed checkout flows. Can you confirm whether this is tied to autoscale warm starts on GPU pools? We also forwarded logs from our side to ops@redwood.com.

Need: immediate mitigation (reduce tail latency) and a short postmortem. We're happy to run traffic-shaping tests if you need a reproducible load.

Thanks,
Helen
SRE, AcuPay

Attachments: acupay-p99-spikes-20260814.png (image), acupay-error-sample-20260814.txt (text)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

On Fri, Aug 14, 2026 at 09:25, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marcus, can you pull warmstart histograms and any recent kernel/JIT errors for the GPU pool that serves AcuPay?

Quick initial findings from edge telemetry and runtime traces:
- Warmstart latency (time from instance spin to first token out) has a 95th of ~2.2s but p99 sits between 8–12s during recent bursts.
- We see correlated queue-growth spikes in the fronting layer when the autoscaler terminates idle instances and starts new ones. Some requests hit the routing cutoff and are retried by the client, producing 502s in the window.
- Root contributors: container init + model KV cache population + CUDA kernel JIT in a subset of older GPU images (happens when instances boot in certain AZs).
- No persistent model corruption; this is a warmstart sequencing and resource contention problem.

Immediate recommend (short-term):
1) Enable 2 prewarmed standby instances in the pool that are kept 'hot' for the morning batch window (08:00–10:00 ET).
2) Temporarily increase autoscaler burst capacity to avoid queue cutoffs while we patch the boot images.
3) Apply a JIT-cache warmup step (small synthetic requests) during instance startup to avoid per-instance kernel compile cross-talk.

I'll push a view with the warmstart histogram and stack traces to the internal telemetry link and prepare a patch for the boot image. Planning to run a controlled rollout to gauge effect.

Marcus
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Intermittent p99 spikes during morning batch — AcuPay production

Thanks Marcus — I'll schedule the standby prewarm for AcuPay's pool and coordinate the burst increase.

Action items (Marissa):
- Enable 2 prewarmed nodes in the AcuPay hosted pool for 08:00–10:00 ET today.
- Increase burst cap by 20% for the next 2 hours and monitor error rate and p99.
- Notify AcuPay SRE when changes are live and recommend a 10-minute smoke test.

Evelyn, Marcus — if we confirm improvement post-change, can we commit to a short-term config change for morning windows while patching the boot image? Also flagged for product/infra roadmap to implement persistent prewarm policies for high-SLO customers.

Marissa
Customer Success (Escalations), Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Intermittent p99 spikes during morning batch — AcuPay production

Hi Helen — quick update:
- We've enabled 2 prewarmed standby instances for your pool and increased burst capacity as a temporary mitigation.
- Marcus has scheduled a JIT-warmup during instance startup and is preparing a boot-image patch to avoid kernel JIT contention.
- Please run a short smoke test (10 minutes) and share the results in this thread or #acupay-prod. We'll keep the temporary config until a validated patch is rolled out (target: 48–72 hours).

Also looping in Rishi for visibility; we may need to discuss a one-off credit if this materially impacted your SLA for today.

Thanks for the patience — we'll push telemetry and a short RCA once the patch is validated.

—David
From: Helen Zhou <hzhou@acupay.com>

Thanks David — we ran the smoke test after your change and saw p99 drop to ~1.1s and 502s return to baseline (~0.02%). That's a clear improvement.

Two asks:
1) Can you share ETA for the boot-image patch and when the prewarm policy will be available as a self-serve setting?
2) Please advise next steps on credit evaluation for the affected window.

Appreciate the fast response from your team.

Helen
SRE, AcuPay
